title: Why Are Bubbles Always Round? #bubbles #physics
description:
Blow through a square wand and you still get a round bubble. Surface tension shrinks the soap film as much as it can, while the air inside pushes back. The shape that holds that air with the least film is a sphere: a cube would need about 24% more.

More on water molecules: Why microwaves don't heat food from the inside https://youtu.be/ri17BZl0Iq8

Sources
- Isenberg (1992), The Science of Soap Films and Soap Bubbles, Dover
- MIT NNF, Bubbles (web.mit.edu/nnf/education/wettability/bubbles.html)
- Virginia Tech Physics, Bubble physics: basic information
- Schwarz (1884), isoperimetric property of the sphere

Try it with a square wand. Did you get a round bubble? Tell me in the comments.
